summary: Ollama silently truncates prompts to its default num_ctx (~4096) and returns HTTP 200 with a plausible wrong answer. Advertised context length (e.g. 131072) is NOT the effective window. Always set num_ctx explicitly per call and assert prompt_eval_count == intended tokens; record evaluated tokens in any trace.
also_seen_in: local_llm wrapper (config.py:16) independently hit and fixed this earlier — repeated across 2 projects

summary: A silently-dropped system prompt (snake_case/camelCase field mismatch) presented as 'the model ignored the format instruction' — a harness fault masquerading as a prompt fault. 'Blame the prompt, not the model' is only safe when the trace proves the model actually received the prompt. Record what the model consumed, not just what you meant to send.
how_to_apply: For any LLM harness: assert the payload actually sent, and make traces show evaluated tokens + the real provider payload so harness faults cannot be misattributed to prompt quality.

summary: MDE view principle: a view must not lose information about identity and connections. A list/summary that collapses a multi-step process to its final state (e.g. showing only the resolving provider and hiding that a call fell over from gemini->openrouter->local) drops the connection that makes the record useful. Show the path/lineage, dim the non-final steps, but never omit them.
origin: Ferosh, reviewing the Cortex trace views 2026-07-29
how_to_apply: When rendering any list/tree/summary of a process that had multiple steps, actors, or handoffs, render the ordered lineage (source->...->resolver), not just the terminal value. Applies to provider fallback paths, job->call grouping, retry chains, ownership/attribution, and any 'who touched this' trail. Carry the ordered data to the client (don't aggregate it away in the query) so the view can show connections.
validator_candidate: a view-review check: 'does any list cell represent a multi-step outcome by a single terminal value?'
